plan.notes: Official eight-semester graduation plan transcribed from purchase.edu (Mathematics/Computer Science > Requirements > Eight-Semester Graduation Plan), fetched 2026-09-30; raw transcription saved in scratch dir. CREDENTIAL HONESTY: Purchase College offers NO standalone Computer Science degree; the true computing degree is the BA in Mathematics/Computer Science (program page shows 'BA / Minor', https://purchase.edu/academics/mathematics-computer-science/). Students choose upper-level electives by track: programming careers take Data Structures, Scripting for the Web, etc.; mathematics track takes Number Theory, Numerical Analysis. Catalog year 2026-2027 = current catalog (plan page updated ~mid-2026; degree requirements page gives 'For Students Entering Fall 2026 and Later' band). Caveats: (1) The published plan does not list MAT 3120 Discrete Mathematics (a Fall 2026+ requirement) or MAT 3880 Junior Seminar in Mathematics/Computer Science (official prereq for MAT 4880) as standalone rows; MAT 3120 is a 3000-level course that may occupy one of the 'MAT 3/4***' slots, and MAT 3880 is carried in external_prereqs with this explanation. (2) The plan shows five 4-credit 'MAT 3/4*** Upper Level Math/CS Elective' slots (20 credits); Fall 2026+ requires four upper-level electives (16 credits) plus MAT 3120. (3) Calculus placement is by faculty interview/transcripts; Precalculus is offered for students lacking the Calculus I background. (4) Grade minima: C or higher in MAT 1500, MAT 1510, MAT 1520, MAT 3120; C- otherwise (excluding senior project). (5) Published semester totals sum to exactly 120 = catalog minimum; upper-level content in the plan totals 45 credits = the 45 upper-level minimum. No courses, credits, or prereqs invented; choice slots transcribed verbatim as student-choice rows.
